error.signature: AI tells a foreigner in Sweden holding a coordination number (samordningsnummer) - even one issued after Skatteverket's in-person 'styrkt identitet' (verified identity) check - that they can obtain Swedish BankID

verdict.summary: BankID, issued only by Swedish banks, requires a full personnummer, not a samordningsnummer of any identity-verification tier. Sweden's Parliament confirmed in October 2024 that no official Swedish photo-ID document yet exists for coordination-number holders and set no timeline for banks to accept a passport as sufficient proof for BankID issuance. The practical route remains obtaining a personnummer via 12-month population registration (folkbokforing), or, for select government e-services only, logging in with a foreign eIDAS-notified eID through Sweden Connect instead of BankID.

dead_ends.action: State or imply that a samordningsnummer - even one issued after Skatteverket's in-person 'styrkt identitet' (verified identity) check - is sufficient to obtain BankID
dead_ends.why_fails: BankID's issuing banks require a full personnummer, not a coordination number of any tier. In a written parliamentary answer dated 30 October 2024, Minister Erik Slottner confirmed no official Swedish photo-ID document yet exists for coordination-number holders and that, due to related EU negotiations, 'a specific timeline cannot currently be provided' for changing this.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 2023 reform introducing the three-tier samordningsnummer system (with 'styrkt identitet' as the top tier) itself unlocked BankID eligibility for coordination-number holders.

workarounds.action: If eligible (planned stay of 12+ months), register with Skatteverket via the 'Flytta till Sverige' e-service as soon as you arrive and complete the required in-person identity check to obtain a personnummer - the standard prerequisite banks require before issuing BankID
If BankID itself is unobtainable, check whether the specific Swedish government e-service accepts login via a foreign eIDAS-notified eID through Sweden Connect / DIGG's eIDAS node instead of BankID
workarounds.how: eIDAS requires Swedish public-sector e-services to offer a login option for notified eIDs issued by other EU/EEA states, proxied through the Swedish eIDAS node - but this covers only eIDAS-connected services, not a general BankID replacement.
workarounds.condition: Holder of an EU/EEA-notified eID needing a specific eIDAS-connected government e-service

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers how and when a personnummer itself is issued; this one covers what BankID access does (and does not) follow from having one, or lacking one.
